correctness.rationale: Kileel's maximal-minor presentation reduces, after a projective normalization of the three independent camera centers and dehomogenization at the known singular point, to a \(4\times3\) matrix whose first two columns can be replaced by their differences with the third. The rank condition is then exactly the rank-at-most-one condition on a \(3\times2\) matrix of six independent linear forms. Exact determinant identities are replayed by the packaged verifier. The Segre degree calculation gives multiplicity \(3\), and the quadratic defining equations give tangent-space dimension \(6\).

value.rationale: The result resolves the precise local type of the only singular point in the three-camera line multiview model. That point is already singled out in the literature as relevant to Euclidean-distance critical-point computations and line-reconstruction sensitivity. Identifying it as a Segre cone gives exact multiplicity, embedding dimension, Hilbert series, and a canonical determinantal normal form; these are structural local invariants rather than a parameter substitution or a recomputation of the published singular-locus statement. The scope is narrow but naturally forced by the unique singular configuration.
